requirements.title: Preserve ordered scroll batches and provide a source-bound Latest action
requirements.spec: Preserve every terminal-delivered wheel step through ordered adjacent-compatible motion segments in the existing finite ready batch, advancing from the evolving source/width-bound logical anchor. Add a current-published-frame Latest button in the existing hint row, sharing an explicit selected-source follow/catch-up action with /view follow; no automatic repin, second writer, new timer or pixel-delta claim.
acceptance: Replace the single overwriteable ScrollRequest with a source-bound pending navigation plan. Capture the actual logical/published starting anchor only on the first movement; subsequent motion advances from that evolving logical position, never resets from visible.first.

Compress adjacent same-direction movements for the same source/pane/geometry with checked count arithmetic. Keep direction changes and pane/source/resize/explicit-anchor changes as semantic barriers. Do not sum an entire burst into one signed net value: at the top, Up then Down must still move down, whereas a zero net sum would incorrectly leave the viewport at the top.

Consume each ordered segment before final frame construction through a geometry-only cached-row advance that returns a final ViewAnchor. Count/skip cached row groups rather than allocating one LogicalRow/PaintRow per travelled row. Visible paint remains bounded by actual viewport height; body/style maps remain source/width/revision-bound.

No new timer, delay, frame rate, velocity multiplier, inertia or queue cap. The plan lives only for the existing finite ready frontier and coalesces runs; it is not a persistent input queue. Preserve every reported terminal wheel step. Current one-row-per-report behavior remains the factual baseline until Tom chooses a separate explicit sensitivity setting.

Non-wheel actions keep original arrival semantics. Explicit follow/anchor replacement clears or resolves earlier pending motion as part of that action, so old scroll work cannot repin the viewport after Latest. Resize keeps logical body/byte anchors, invalidates old row geometry and establishes a new geometry barrier. Source replacement cancels old motion explicitly.

Wheel targets stay independent: Conversation changes its logical anchor; Diff/Agents changes its own list offset; popup selection remains popup-owned; composer wheel behavior remains existing behavior. A mixed-pane burst never merges two targets.

Keep unknown history/body boundaries honest. This row does not pretend unloaded bytes are known rows or add eager whole-history/body reads. Existing explicit older/more requests remain available; any future automatic boundary demand requires its own precise registered behavior.

Display the exact label ↓ Latest when the conversation viewport is pinned/not following, demonstrably away from tail, or an explicit latest catch-up is pending. Normal following tail has no button. A pin at the visible bottom may still offer resuming follow; this is deliberate.

Place it right-aligned in the existing final composer hint row, with normal measured terminal-cell widths. Reserve its rectangle before clipping remaining hints. No header/footer/new row, reduced composer width or overlay over transcript text.

At widths that cannot show the complete label, omit it and its hit region; /view follow remains available. When it fits, show the whole label and prevent overlap with send-key toggle, upcoming target label and other active hit regions. Never leave a clipped or hidden clickable region.

The button is generated chrome with no original-body copy capability. Its hit region carries current selected source/publication identity and becomes authoritative only after terminal write+flush succeeds. Clear it on failed publication, no-paint, resize or source replacement; queued clicks cannot activate an old target.

Click invokes the shared typed follow-latest action used by /view follow. It does not send text, change agent execution, steal composer focus, submit/clear the draft or silently replace selected agent. Preserve original selected-body capability for copy/export according to existing follow behavior.
Integrate with NUI004 drag selection through one owner of published hit regions; button hits take precedence only inside their exact non-overlapping rectangle.

Extract one follow_latest action: clear earlier pending navigation, call existing Viewport::follow_tail, mark the frame dirty, and request a source-bound catch-up outside paint. /view follow and mouse use the same path.

Reuse configured history_demand and newer_history from the highest observed page cursor. One active history job at a time; if an older read is pending, retain one explicit latest request until completion rather than swallowing the click. Capture the first actual read snapshot’s accepted event frontier and catch up to it using bounded pages, with each completion yielding to the event loop. No eager whole-history clone or invented page count.

When no prior history cursor exists, reuse the existing bounded initial tail demand. Preserve explicit unloaded-body continuation notices; Latest means the latest admitted conversation item, not secretly downloading every byte of a large body.

An empty After result for a nonempty store must correctly prove the requested frontier has been reached; do not rely only on accept_history’s current empty-store arm. Keep sparse/unavailable coverage explicit and never label merely loaded old history as current.

If the operator scrolls or changes target while catch-up is pending, accepted records may populate their valid source projection, but completion must not restore follow, steal focus, clear a newer draft or paint another source. User navigation cancels only the follow intent; normal canonical observation remains valid.

Attempt dirty frame publication on history/body/input completion in the active turn loop as well as the idle loop; do not make new navigation wait for the120fps status tick. Keep the existing status cadence unchanged in this row. A later idle-timer redesign is not needed to fix the lost steps.
Bind the action to the selected view/read handle when target switching is integrated. Never hardcode the root store for a button displayed over a child view.

First reproduce the old failure using actual App input batching: N same-direction SGR wheel reports in one ready batch must move exactly N available rows, matching individually published reports. Run idle and during MockProvider streaming.

After the semantic repair, compare fixed identical bursts and isolated steps on the same terminal size/source. Capture input receipt to successful frame publication latency, total bytes/write/flush counts, elapsed/CPU and final top anchor or numbered visible row. Report median/tail measurements without inventing a performance threshold or claiming pixel fidelity.

Separate warm loaded/cache-hit scrolling, first-entry body demand, reverse movement after existing cache eviction, large tool/Markdown body and width change. Preserve actual body-map Arc identity on warm same-width steps in unit tests; show no parser/layout rebuild or body/store I/O was requested by a cache hit.

Keep retained changed-cell output and one writer. Full frame preparation/changed-cell scanning and cold body reparse are candidates to measure, not established dominant costs. Do not add terminal scroll-region commands, a second writer, arbitrary overscan memory or an animation subsystem without fresh evidence.
Native trackpad feel still needs a human terminal check because SGR PTY reports model terminal-delivered wheel steps, not the OS’s fractional gesture data. Preserve current API limitations honestly.

api_contracts: PendingNavigation::push(source, pane, geometry, direction, rows) -> Result; compress adjacent compatible runs, preserve ordered barriers; take consumes one finite batch.
render::navigation::advance_cached(...) -> Result<NavigationOutcome>; returns final source-bound anchor or explicit loaded-boundary/stale outcome without materializing traversed paint rows.
view_actions::latest::follow_latest(&mut AppState) -> Result<(),TuiError>; shared by command and mouse, records explicit source-bound demand and clears pending motion.
LatestHit { area, source, publication_owner }; prepared alongside the frame, committed only on successful publication; no public caller-minted identity.
Transcript::load_newer_for_latest(...) uses the existing supervised HistoryRead job surface and configured count; only the current follow request owns the captured catch-up frontier.
focused_tests: Actual pending plan and cached advance:1,12 and large finite wheel bursts; same output as per-event execution; mixed direction at both boundaries; alternating panes; checked count overflow.
Wheel then /view follow in one finite batch; follow then wheel; resize interleaving; body revision replacement; source change. No stale motion or original-byte rebind.
Button absent while following, present while pinned, exact cell bounds in wide/narrow panes, no overlapping send button, hide on insufficient width, source change or failed write/flush.

Click Latest during streaming and during old-history read; one source-bound current-frontier demand; empty current-tail page; append during catch-up; late completion after manual scroll or target switch.

Actual App PTY numbered multi-page transcript: rapid SGR up/down, streaming output while pinned, click visible Latest, observe newest marker, then narrow/wide resize and verify composer draft/focus and terminal restoration.
Actual wide-grapheme/combining Markdown and Diff/Agents scrolling retain source maps; controls remain escaped; chrome never yields body copy bytes.
